skill.name: backend-api
skill.description: Guides design and implementation of RESTful API routes, controllers, versioning, query parameters, status codes, and rate limiting.
skill.summary: Guides REST API endpoint design and implementation with practical backend conventions.
skill.author: DevanB

security_audit.summary: Four shell-execution findings are false positives caused by Markdown inline code around paths and API examples. The relative link using parent-directory traversal is a real filesystem concern because it directs the agent outside the skill package.

remediation.suggestion: Package the referenced backend API standard inside the skill directory or replace the parent-directory link with self-contained instructions.
Keep path examples as plain Markdown examples, but avoid wording that could be mistaken for executable shell instructions.

static_findings.snippet: - When creating or editing API route definitions in `routes/api.php` or similar routing files
- When building or modifying controllers in `app/Http/Controllers/` or controller directories
- When building or modifying API controllers in `app/Http/Controllers/Api/` or API-specific controll
- When implementing API versioning (URL path versioning like `/api/v1/` or header-based versioning)

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 12 uses Markdown inline code to name routes/api.php. It does not instruct Ruby, shell, or command execution.
Line 13 uses Markdown inline code to name a controller directory. No command invocation or dynamic execution is present.
Line 14 uses Markdown inline code to describe an API controller path. The backticks are formatting, not executable syntax.
Line 17 formats /api/v1/ as an inline API path example. It is not shell syntax and does not execute commands.
Line 27 links to ../../../agent-os/standards/backend/api.md, which escapes the skill directory. This can prompt filesystem access outside the packaged skill boundary.

high_findings.title: Path traversal sequence
high_findings.confidence_reasoning: Line 27 links to ../../../agent-os/standards/backend/api.md, which escapes the skill directory. This can prompt filesystem access outside the packaged skill boundary.

content.value_statement: Backend API work often needs consistent routes, controllers, status codes, and query handling. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through practical REST API design choices.
actual_capabilities: Guides RESTful route design for backend API endpoints.
Supports controller and API controller implementation patterns.
Helps choose HTTP methods and response status codes.
Covers API versioning with path or header strategies.
Provides guidance for filtering, sorting, pagination, and search parameters.
Addresses rate limiting headers and throttling decisions.
limitations: It references an external standards file outside the skill package.
It does not include complete framework-specific implementation code.
It focuses on REST APIs, not GraphQL or event-driven APIs.
It requires project context to match existing route and controller conventions.

use_cases.title: Create New API Endpoints
use_cases.description: Design resource routes, controller actions, and response codes for a new backend feature.

use_cases.title: Refine API Structure
use_cases.description: Review route names, URL structure, versioning, and query parameters for consistency.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Guidance
use_cases.description: Apply shared REST API conventions during code generation or review.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Basic Endpoint
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for one resource endpoint.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the backend-api skill to design a REST endpoint for managing projects. Include route, method, controller action, and response status.

prompt_templates.title: Add Query Controls
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the backend-api skill to add filtering, sorting, pagination, and search parameters to an existing users endpoint.

prompt_templates.title: Review API Conventions
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of existing backend routes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the backend-api skill to review these API routes for RESTful structure, status codes, and controller naming consistency.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Versioned API Changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the backend-api skill to plan a versioned API change from v1 to v2, including compatibility, routing, and response behavior.

output_examples.output: A concise endpoint plan with resource routes, HTTP methods, controller responsibilities, and expected success and error responses.
A review summary covering query parameter names, pagination behavior, status codes, and consistency with REST conventions.

output_examples.input: Plan API versioning for breaking changes.
output_examples.output: A migration outline that compares path and header versioning, then recommends a rollout approach.

best_practices: Provide existing route and controller patterns before asking for changes.
Ask for explicit HTTP methods, status codes, and error behavior.
Review generated endpoints against project authorization and validation rules.
anti_patterns: Do not use it as a complete security review for API authentication.
Do not request broad rewrites without sharing current route conventions.
Do not assume the external standards link is available in every installation.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps design and implement REST API routes, controllers, versioning, query parameters, status codes, and rate limits.

faq.question: Does it support Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is it specific to Laravel?
faq.answer: It references Laravel-style paths, but the REST API guidance can apply to similar backend frameworks.

faq.question: Can it generate complete production code?
faq.answer: It can guide implementation, but production code still needs project context, tests, validation, and security review.

faq.question: What security issue was found?
faq.answer: The skill links to a parent-directory documentation path that may escape the packaged skill boundary.

faq.question: How should authors fix the issue?
faq.answer: Authors should include the referenced API standard inside the skill package or make the guidance self-contained.
